messages:
deepak: FYI bringing up osprey-12b int4 on staging. quant build looks fine but we hit repeated OOMs when we bump concurrent requests beyond 2. logs show tons of small free/alloc churn, might be fragmentation.
jen: Can you paste the exact command/config you used? batch_size, max_new_tokens default?
maria: Also which allocator are you on (tcmalloc/jemalloc/ptmalloc)? fragmentation patterns differ.
deepak: Using the regular runtime image + our int4 kernel. config: `batch_size: 4, max_new_tokens: 512, kv_cache: enabled, prefetch: true, prefetch_window: 32` allocator looks like ptmalloc (glibc).
noah: That prefetch_window looks aggressive for 12b int4, can spike working set due to KV shadowing. Try prefetch_window: 8 and set batch_size: 2 as an experiment.
sara: Also try lowering max_new_tokens default for this model in the serving profiles to 256 — many of our conversations don't need 512 and it reduces peak seq length.
deepak: good call. changed prefetch_window->8 and max_new_tokens->256, restarted. still saw one OOM at ~45s, then it stabilized. attaching snippet of the allocator trace we get right before crash:
```
malloc_consolidate(): top size 0x1e0000
malloc: can't allocate region
--- GLIBC malloc debug ---
free chunk: prev_size=0x40 size=0x90
malloc: arenas[2] got corrupted
```
jen: that screams fragmentation exacerbated by large sparse KV buffers. On int4 we compact less well because kernels keep many small objects.
maria: Could we enable KV trim on idle or reduce per-request KV reserve? There's a runtime flag `--kv-reserve-pages` that defaults to 12 for 12b; drop it to 6 to test.
noah: Another quick workaround: enable ephemeral caching for prefixes so long-lived prefix caches don't pin pages. `cache.policy=ephemeral` for this model route.
deepak: toggled kv-reserve to 6 and ephemeral cache. after a few hours on staging throughput is fine, no OOMs seen. latency slightly higher for long contexts but within SLO.
sara: Great. For rollout plan: 1) keep model in staging with kv-reserve=6 + prefetch_window=8 + max_new_tokens=256 for 48h, 2) run synthetic long-context burst test (100 concurrent with 256 new tokens) 3) if stable, promote to canary at 5% with same profile.
deepak: I'll run the synthetic job now and dump flamegraphs. quick question: should we also try jemalloc build? Could reduce fragmentation.
maria: Yes, compile-test with jemalloc is worth it. It's a bit of an engineering lift but if the fragmentation persists it's the long-term fix.
ci-bot: build/4567 queued: osprey-12b-int4+jemalloc test build started.
noah: If jemalloc reduces RSS variance, we can keep higher prefetch_window for throughput. Keep an eye on p99 mem+latency tradeoff.
sara: Document the final serving profile in the model catalog entry (model: osprey-12b, quant: int4, profile: prefetch=8, kv-reserve=6, max_new_tokens=256, allocator=ptmalloc/jemalloc-note). Also add regression test for mem fragmentation.
deepak: will update the model catalog and link the synthetic job results. thanks all :thumbsup:
